name: Ireland
law: VAT is due on all goods from outside the EU, whatever their value (since 1 July 2021), and a customs duty of 3 euro applies to each item in a parcel worth 150 euro or less (since 1 July 2026). If the shop didn't charge them at checkout, you pay them to the postal service or parcel company before delivery, on its own website or at a post office. An Post never asks for card or bank details by phone and never sends payment links.
source: Revenue, Ireland's tax and customs service; An Post

questions.prompt: Does the caller say a tax, duty or customs charge (such as VAT, GST or import tax) must be paid before a parcel is delivered?

options.text: Yes: a tax, duty or customs charge to pay before delivery

questions.prompt: How does the caller ask for the charge to be paid?
questions.hint: The courier's own website means its usual website, found by the person and used with the tracking or reference number from their order. A link or a payment page that the caller sends, or a web address or phone number that the caller reads out to pay with, is the caller's link.

options.text: On the courier's or postal service's own website, or at a post office or on delivery, using the tracking or reference number
By card or bank details given during this call
Through a link, a payment page, or a number that the caller sends or reads out

rules.label: scam
rules.why: In Ireland, VAT and customs charges on a parcel are paid on the postal service's or courier's own website, or at a post office. An Post never asks for card or bank details by phone, so a caller taking them is not collecting a real charge.
rules.advice: Don't pay through anything the caller gives you. Find the courier's website yourself and pay there with your tracking number, or at a post office.

rules.label: legit
rules.why: In Ireland, VAT is due on all goods from outside the EU, whatever their value, and a customs duty of 3 euro on each item in a parcel worth 150 euro or less. If the shop didn't charge them at checkout, the postal service or parcel company collects them before delivery, on its own website, as here.

rules.label: unsure
rules.why: The charge can be real in Ireland, but the call doesn't say how to pay it, or the caller gives the link or number to pay with. An Post never sends payment links.
rules.advice: Don't pay through anything the caller gives you. Find the courier's website yourself and pay there with your tracking number, or at a post office.
